placements.title: Commanded Erasure and Corrective Replacement
placements.frame: What pattern emerges when directives to purge specific knowledge are paired with authoritative claims about what never happened?
placements.why: All three expressions enact a single thematic pattern: imperatives commanding the erasure of specific knowledge (Kestrelwood spectrograph, 88.4 MHz calibration, Quill Ashgrove's calibration work) followed by a flat corrective assertion that replaces what was purged with a negation of the original claim. This is a thematic subject future envelopes could feed — other suppression directives, other corrective replacements — not a one-time fact. The grain test holds: the pattern of commanding erasure and supplying replacement narrative is true beyond these specific words.
